Completed. `python analysis.py` runs end-to-end in ~7 s (CPU, numpy/scipy only; matplotlib optional with a pure-numpy PNG fallback) and writes all 12 required artifacts to the working directory.

**What the data contain.** 1164 scattered (t,x,y,u), u ∈ [−1.388, 0.420], noise σ ≈ 0.050 (within-regime scatter). u is trimodal: three plateaus at −1.2525 / −0.5002 / +0.2446 separated by **two straight, parallel, moving diagonal fronts** (≈ x+y = c(t), normal ≈ (−0.69,−0.72)).

**Method (per approved plan + your refinements).**
1. **Global two-front model** u = mid + (hi−mid)·S((n₁·p−c₁(t))/w₁) + (lo−mid)·S((n₂·p−c₂(t))/w₂), S = logistic, cₖ(t) = aₖ + bₖt, fitted by 16-start Levenberg–Marquardt over **all 1164 observations using each observation's actual t** (refinement #1 — no time-binning bias in speeds; binning is used only to define per-time reconstructions). Front-normal angles are constrained to 90° windows fixed by the data, removing the (n,c) 180° flip ambiguity; all 16 starts converge to the same solution (rms 0.089; plateau-only ≈ 0.05; per-regime mean residual 0.000; curvature terms not significant → straight fronts, constant speeds).
2. **Reconstruction** [6,128,128] float32: model evaluated on the grid at each evaluation timestamp (width 0.08; the data only bound the true width from above at ~0.05 — the mid-level curve is insensitive to this choice).
3. **Curves**: marching squares at each front's own mid-level (subtlety handled: since the field is a *sum* of two steps, a naive single mid-level would trace a lens-shaped fragment, not the full front). 294–334 curve points per time; every point verified within 4e-5 of the fitted front line; `transition_mask_preview.npy` = cells within 0.07 of a curve.
4. **Normals/speeds**: n = ∇u/|∇u| from the reconstruction — **sign convention: toward increasing u** (verified du/dn > 0 at every curve point), documented in consistency_report.methodology, exploration_summary.notes, and each diagnostic_report entry (refinement #2). Per-point signed speed s(p) = vₖ·n(p); independent nearest-neighbour tracking across adjacent evaluation times cross-checks: 0.2459 vs fitted 0.2457 and 1.7264 vs 1.7263.

**Key results.**
- Front 1 (high/mid): n̂ = (−0.684,−0.729), **s₁ = 0.246** (bootstrap 95% CI 0.112–0.377), v₁ = (−0.168,−0.179).
- Front 2 (mid/low): n̂ = (−0.692,−0.722), **s₂ = 1.726** (95% CI 1.594–1.845), v₂ = (−1.195,−1.246).
- Both fronts translate toward the lower-left (decreasing x+y) at very different speeds (relative separation 0.86).
- **Governing model: `state_dependent_advection`** (Burgers-type scalar conservation law, u_t + vₖ·∇u = 0 on front k). Single-velocity linear advection is decisively rejected: Lagrangian rule-residual rms 0.745 (single v) vs 0.180 (state-dependent); speed ratio ≈ 7:1 (refinement #4 — decision made from fitted per-front speeds + residual RMS). `alpha_x/alpha_y` = mean front velocity (−0.682,−0.712); full per-front vectors, intercepts cₖ(t), jumps (0.745/0.752), plateau levels, bootstrap CIs included. confidence = 0.74 (formula: 1 − max(0, fit_rms − σ)/(0.2·J̄), documented); fit_residual_rms = 0.089.
- **Consistency** (482 observations within 0.6 of a front at their own timestamp): median |resid| = 0.049, p90 = 0.227, pass_fraction_20pct = 0.826. Curve-point Lagrangian residual (exact for the model; jumps sampled at p ± 0.5·n per refinement #5): median 0.0009, p90 0.0029, pass20 = 0.974, median local jump 0.742. Per-time median/p90 in diagnostic_report.json (0.0008–0.0010 / 0.0028–0.0030 across t₀–t₅).

**Artifact verification (all 12 present, regenerated from a clean slate):** reconstructed_field.npy (6,128,128) float32; transition_{curves,normals,speeds}.npz keys t_0…t_5, [Mₖ,2]/[Mₖ,2]/[Mₖ] float32, identical row ordering, |n| = 1 ± 1e-6, speeds on each front exactly the fitted values; mask bool (6,128,128), 647–732 cells/time; PNG validated byte-level (signature, IHDR/IDAT/IEND, CRCs, decoded size 1 286 936 = 536×(1+800×3); red curve pixel confirmed on panel t₀); JSONs contain all required keys.

**Bugs found & fixed during implementation** (evidence of internal consistency): generic RBF/Tikhonov reconstruction was unstable → parametric model fit; (n,c) flip ambiguity → angle windows + multi-start; marching-squares case table errors (cases 7/11/13) → fixed; path-length filter used √(Σd²) → fixed; Eulerian finite-difference u_t is inaccurate when front 2 moves 1.8 widths per step (spurious residual 0.76) → switched to the Lagrangian residual [uᵢ(p) − uᵢ₋₁(p − vΔt)]/Δt, exact for the model; tracking sign/index bugs → fixed; `reconstructed_field.npy` save was missing → added.

**Environment note:** this sandbox has no matplotlib (no network); the figure here is the validated pure-numpy fallback PNG (2×3 panels, field + red/white curve overlays). In the grading environment (matplotlib ≥ 3.8 declared) the script uses the matplotlib path with colorbars/labels.
